label: SYNTHETIC TRAINING CASES — NO LIVE TELEMETRY
notice: Every person, host, address, message, and event in these exercises is fictional and fabricated. KQL snippets are illustrative and have not been run against a tenant. A match is a lead for investigation, not proof of compromise.

cases.title: Repeated sign-in failures followed by success
cases.alert: A synthetic account has several failed sign-ins followed by one successful sign-in from a source marked unfamiliar in the mock baseline.
facts: Nine failed sign-in events (synthetic ResultType 50126) occurred over eight minutes, followed by one successful event (ResultType 0).
The mock exercise labels the source as unfamiliar; there is no real user or trusted location baseline attached.
MFA details, device compliance, user confirmation, token activity, and other accounts touched by the source are not yet known.
hypotheses: Possible password guessing or credential use followed by account access; success and failures need identity-owner corroboration.
Possible expected VPN, travel, shared egress, stale credentials, or a service/app pattern; location unfamiliarity alone is not malicious proof.
investigate: Confirm account owner, expected travel/VPN, app, device, authentication method, MFA result, and whether the successful event was recognized.
Pivot on the source and time window to determine whether multiple accounts were targeted; compare related interactive and non-interactive sign-in sources where available.
Record event IDs, time zone, observed facts, unknowns, and the identity-team ticket/owner. Escalate suspected unauthorized success under the incident process.
cases.query_context: Sentinel / Log Analytics workspace with the Entra ID sign-in connector. This query is an unexecuted example; confirm table availability, schema, permissions, and retention first.
cases.kql:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where (UserPrincipalName =~ "analyst1@example.invalid" or IPAddress == "203.0.113.42")
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, IPAddress, Location, IsInteractive, ResultType, ResultDescription
| take 100

actions.title: Keep open and gather corroborating identity evidence
actions.feedback: Appropriate if the identity owner and incident lead classify this as lower risk, but the unexplained successful sign-in after repeated failures must remain tracked.

actions.title: Escalate the possible unauthorized success; validate in parallel
actions.feedback: Recommended for this exercise: the successful sign-in after repeated failures is a credible account-risk signal. Escalation is not proof of compromise and does not itself authorize account changes.

actions.title: Close as benign based on unfamiliar location alone
actions.feedback: Not supported. An unfamiliar source does not prove maliciousness, but the unverified successful sign-in and missing MFA/device/user evidence mean closure is premature.

cases.closure_criteria: Close only after an authorized reviewer documents trusted sign-in evidence, user/device confirmation, the disposition, and any required follow-up; use approved containment authority if compromise is supported.
cases.safety_boundary: Do not reset credentials, revoke sessions, block an IP, or contact the address based only on this exercise. Follow the incident lead and identity team's authorization process.

references.title: Microsoft Learn: Send Microsoft Entra ID data to Microsoft Sentinel

cases.title: Encoded PowerShell launched by an office application
cases.alert: A synthetic endpoint alert identifies an encoded PowerShell command whose reported initiating process is WINWORD.EXE.
facts: The toy event records PowerShell with an encoded-command switch and WINWORD.EXE as the initiating process.
The command payload is intentionally omitted; the exercise contains no executable payload or real endpoint telemetry.
No signer/hash reputation, parent document origin, child-process or network events, user activity, or managed-device baseline is supplied.
hypotheses: Possible malicious document-driven script execution; parent-child context is concerning and needs prompt escalation under the endpoint playbook.
Possible approved macro, administrative automation, or test tool; encoded text and a process name alone do not establish intent or impact.
investigate: Preserve the event and correlate by ProcessUniqueId, device, account, timestamp, parent/child processes, file/hash/signature, and approved change or software records.
Check related endpoint detections, network connections, file writes, other devices/users, and whether the device is managed and reachable.
Notify the endpoint incident owner promptly. Any isolation, evidence collection, or remediation must use the approved authority and evidence-preservation procedure.
cases.query_context: Microsoft Defender XDR advanced hunting (or an appropriately connected Sentinel environment). This query is an unexecuted example, not a synthetic tenant result. DeviceProcessEvents requires Defender for Endpoint telemetry; confirm the actual schema before use.
cases.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where DeviceName =~ "LAB-WS-01"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessUniqueId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| take 100

actions.title: Preserve and correlate endpoint evidence while keeping the case open
actions.feedback: Evidence correlation is essential, but given the reported office-app-to-encoded-PowerShell chain, notify the endpoint incident owner promptly rather than treating this as routine low-priority review.

actions.title: Promptly escalate to the endpoint incident owner and preserve evidence
actions.feedback: Recommended for this exercise: the parent-child pattern merits urgent analyst review. Escalation does not mean the activity is confirmed malicious or authorize endpoint isolation.

actions.title: Close because the command is encoded
actions.feedback: Unsupported. Encoding is neither proof of malware nor proof of safety. The parent process and missing context require investigation.

cases.closure_criteria: Close only when an authorized reviewer correlates the event with trusted endpoint evidence and documents a supported benign explanation or completed incident handling, owner, and disposition.
cases.safety_boundary: Never run or decode an unknown payload for this exercise. Do not isolate a device, delete files, or disable an account without approved incident authority.

cases.title: User-reported credential lure with unknown exposure
cases.source: Microsoft Defender XDR email investigation exercise
cases.alert: A synthetic user report and mock gateway record flag a credential-themed message. Delivery state, recipient scope, and link interaction are not yet confirmed.
facts: The toy report has a credential-verification subject, mismatched display and sender context, and a mock gateway Phish label.
The sample event does not establish whether the message was delivered, clicked, replied to, or seen by additional recipients.
Sender and recipient domains are reserved examples; there are no live URLs, mailbox contents, or user identities.
hypotheses: Possible credential-harvesting campaign; determine delivery, recipients, user action, and any associated sign-in activity using approved tools.
Possible mistaken or outdated gateway verdict, simulated test, or legitimate business message; confirm with trusted mail telemetry and the business owner.
investigate: Use the message identifier to inspect the latest trusted delivery/threat state and identify affected recipients; account for multiple records when verdict or delivery changes.
Ask the reporter privately whether they clicked, replied, entered credentials, or approved an MFA request; correlate approved URL-click and sign-in telemetry if available.
Coordinate search/quarantine, user notification, credential/session actions, and evidence preservation with the mail/security owner and incident lead.
cases.query_context: Microsoft Defender XDR advanced hunting. This query is an unexecuted example, not a synthetic tenant result. EmailEvents depends on Defender for Office 365 telemetry; confirm connector, table, and current delivery-state semantics before use.
cases.kql:
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where NetworkMessageId == "SYNTH-MSG-003"
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, ThreatTypes, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
| take 100

actions.title: Keep the case open and establish delivery, click, and recipient scope
actions.feedback: These are necessary pivots. Because the mock gateway flags a credential-themed report, involve the mail/security owner while checking exposure rather than waiting to close the alert.

actions.title: Escalate to the mail/security owner; establish exposure and scope
actions.feedback: Recommended for this exercise: a possible credential lure warrants prompt owner review. A gateway label is a signal, not proof, and containment remains authorized-owner work.

actions.title: Close because no click is recorded in the supplied facts
actions.feedback: No click evidence was supplied; that is an unknown, not a negative result. Establish recipient and user-action scope before closure.

cases.closure_criteria: Document the trusted final message state, recipients and exposure checks, reporter response, any correlated identity evidence, owner-approved actions, and reviewer disposition.
cases.safety_boundary: Do not click the message URL, submit message content to public scanners, purge mail, or change accounts based only on this synthetic case. Use approved tools and delegated authority.
